REASON FOR REFERRAL
38-year-old man with (1) a changing pigmented lesion L upper back and (2) multiple scaly lesions on face and dorsal hands. Lesion noticed "getting darker" over 3 months; overview photos taken at home by partner Summer on 13/9. Last full skin check Mar-2024 (no concerns). BCC excised R shoulder in 2019 (histology attached). FHx: father - melanoma in his 50s.
Sun exposure: surfing most mornings at Currumbin Alley since his teens, rarely reapplies sunscreen; several bad burns this summer. SPF 50+ at work "most days".

O/E (GP)
Lesion A - L upper back (scapular): 7 x 5 mm, asymmetric, two shades of brown with a grey-blue area at the 2 o'clock edge; measured 4 mm on the 03/2025 practice photo. 7-point checklist 3/7.
Lesions B-E - forehead, L temple, dorsum both hands: 3-6 mm rough erythematous scaly papules.
Nails: no longitudinal melanonychia; Hutchinson's sign negative. No cervical/axillary lymphadenopathy.

IMAGE METADATA
Overview: IMG_4471.HEIC, IMG_4472.HEIC (patient's own iPhone 13)
Dermoscopy: DERM-0914-03.jpg, DERM-0914-04.jpg (DermLite DL4, S/N DL4-2209-57731, polarised)
Uploaded 2026-09-14 19:42 AEST via https://skinrefer.tele.example.au/c/7Hq2XZ - quality adequate, ruler in frame for lesion A.

e-CONSULT RESPONSE - Dr Mai Nguyen-Tran, Consultant Dermatologist, Gold Coast University Hospital (16/09/26)
Lesion A: asymmetry of structure and colour, focal regression and blue-white veil on dermoscopy. Melanoma cannot be excluded - excisional biopsy with 2 mm margins within 2 weeks (GP may proceed; no shave biopsy). Send histology to the TD inbox.
Lesions B-E: actinic keratoses. Cryotherapy to isolated lesions, or 5-FU 5% cream bd for 3 weeks to forehead/temple.
Advice: rash vest and wide-brim hat when surfing; annual full skin check given BCC history and FHx.
Outcome: telehealth review after histology.

dialogue:
[doctor] Hello, can you both hear me? I'm Dr Ó Dálaigh, skin registrar in Drogheda. Dr Bowen sent us your photos.
[daughter] We can. I'm Gráinne, her daughter. I'm a nurse up in the Lourdes myself, so I set up the call.
[doctor] Grand. Is it Mrs Ní Mhurchú?
[patient] Everyone calls me Bridie, doctor.
[doctor] Bridie it is. Your date of birth?
[patient] The second of March, nineteen thirty-three. I'm ninety-three, if you'd believe it.
[doctor] And still at home in Clogherhead?
[patient] Harbour View, same house since I married. I taught in Scoil Mhuire in Termonfeckin for thirty years.
[doctor] You've very fair skin, what we call Fitzpatrick type one. Tell me about the patch on the left shin.
[patient] Came up in the spring. Flat, pinky-red, scaly, weeps if the tights rub it. No pain.
[daughter] It's bigger. Aoife, the nurse at the surgery, took the photos on the twenty-first of September.
[doctor] They came through well. It looks most like Bowen's disease, a very early skin cancer in the top layer only. We'll confirm it with a small biopsy at the surgery, then cream or freezing usually sorts it.
[daughter] And the brown crusty ones on her back?
[doctor] Seborrhoeic keratoses, harmless. I'll send you a copy of the letter.
[daughter] Use gkavanagh74@gmail.com, or ring 087 214 6639.
